message.reasoning:
We need to decide whether to bid or drop out. Current high bid 198 by p2. We have cash 680. Property is Pennsylvania Railroad, unowned currently. Owning all 4 railroads is valuable; currently we own Reading Railroad, others own B&O and Short Line (p2 has B&O and Short Line). So there are 4 railroads: Reading (owned by us), Pennsylvania (up for auction), B&O (owned by p2), Short Line (owned by p2). So if we win Pennsylvania, we will have 2 railroads (Reading + Pennsylvania). If p2 gets it, they'd have 3 railroads (B&O, Short Line, Pennsylvania). That's huge advantage for p2. So we likely want to outbid p2 to prevent them from getting 3 railroads. But we also consider cash: we have 680, can afford. Minimum next bid 199. We could bid something like 250 to signal seriousness. But we need to consider future auctions: other properties still unowned many. We have decent cash. Might want to win this to block p2. Could also consider bidding high enough to discourage p2 from further bidding. Since p2 currently leads with 198, we could bid 300. That would cost us 300 cash, leaving 380. Still okay. But we might want to conserve cash for houses later. However railroads are good passive income. Having 2 railroads yields 25*2=50 rent when opponent lands. That's decent.

Given p2 already has 2 railroads, if they get a third, they'd get 75 rent. That's strong. So we should outbid.

Thus we choose to bid. Choose amount maybe 250. Public message could be something like "I bid $250". Private thought: reasoning.

Make tool call bid_auction with bid_amount 250, public_message, private_thought.
